verdict: Bengaluru is decisively heating up in mid-2026: ~24% YoY price growth and ~33% YoY sales jump put it out of step with a softer pan-India market. Fundamentals are still sound — inventory overhang has actually tightened to ~12 months, housing GNPAs remain low at ~1.3%, and the repo rate is comfortable at 5.25% — but launch mix is now ~68% premium/luxury, the asking-vs-registry gap forced a 6–15% guidance-value hike, and affordability is being stretched by the price surge. Risk skews to a luxury-segment air pocket if rates rise or IT hiring softens, since mid-income supply has thinned.

indicators.name: Unsold inventory overhang
indicators.note: Bengaluru overhang at ~12 months on ~58,900 unsold units — well below the 18–24 month healthy benchmark. Q1 2026 sales +33% YoY (15,603 units) and supply-sales near parity have tightened the market further.

indicators.name: Launch mix skew to luxury
indicators.note: High-end and luxury accounted for ~68% of Bengaluru launches in Q1 2026; mid-segment fell to ~31%. Affordable supply has nearly disappeared and 'early fatigue' is being flagged in the ultra-premium segment.
indicators.src: PropTiger Real Insight Q1 2026 / Business Standard

indicators.name: EMI-to-income (affordability)
indicators.note: Knight Frank's index shows Bengaluru affordability comfortably under the 50% stress line, but 24% YoY price growth is now outpacing income growth and eroding the cushion. Repo steady at 5.25%; home loan rates 7.65–8.50%.
indicators.src: Knight Frank India Affordability Index H1 2026

indicators.name: Housing-loan defaults (NPAs)
indicators.note: RBI Financial Stability Report (Dec 2025) shows retail housing GNPA stable at ~1.3% with no significant systemic risk. Watch unsecured retail at 1.7% — slippages there could spill over if rates rise. No public locality-level default data.

indicators.name: Asking vs registered price gap
indicators.value: Guidance values revised up 6–15% Feb 2026 to close gap
indicators.note: Karnataka hiked guidance values 6–15% in Feb 2026 because the gap to actual transaction prices had widened materially in East and North Bengaluru. Registration fee also doubled (1% → 2%) in Aug 2025 — both signs of an overheated transaction market the state is moving to capture.

indicators.name: Registration volumes
indicators.value: Bengaluru sales +33% YoY in Q1 2026 (15,603 units)
indicators.note: Bengaluru is the only major metro with simultaneous peak sequential sales growth and 24% YoY price appreciation. Registration fee hike and guidance-value revision boost state collections, but velocity at these prices is a classic late-cycle froth signal.
